result:
The proposed answer of 7 is not verified, and its key step looks wrong.

**The paw step fails.** The proposal says the paw is in $\mathcal P$ because every subdivision of the paw contains an induced pan. But a subdivision of the paw is a cycle of length at least 3 with a pendant path attached, and most of these are not pans. More importantly, large grids are triangle-free and have unbounded clique-width. A large grid contains an induced cycle with a vertex outside it adjacent to exactly one cycle vertex, which is an induced subdivision of the paw. So graphs with no induced subdivision of the paw do not obviously have bounded clique-width, and the paw likely does not belong to $\mathcal P$. The proposal itself concedes that the pan-free step is unproven and that it did not check a published classification.

**The $K_3+K_1$ step is also doubtful.** Its subdivisions include an induced cycle plus a vertex far away from it. Large grids contain such configurations, so $K_3+K_1$ probably fails as well. Even so, the proposal does not settle that case.

**The edge-count set depends on the membership of several graphs.** The answer 7 requires the paw to be in $\mathcal M$. Since that is doubtful, the set of edge counts (and therefore the sum) is not established by this argument. I could not pin down the correct family $\mathcal M$ from memory, so I cannot give the right value.

Because the central membership claim appears to be false and the final value depends on it, I cannot accept 7.

VERDICT: REJECT
